title: Same counties, same year, five different answers
subtitle: Estimated difference in applied herbicide mass per hectare of harvested cropland associated with a county having 10 percentage points more of its tilled cropland in no-till (US counties, 2017). The only thing that changes between rows is which counties are treated as comparable.

x.label: % difference in applied mass per hectare, per +10 pp no-till share

y.label: Comparison group
y.note: Row 1 compares every county to every other county. Row 5 compares a county only to its neighbours inside the same USDA Crop Reporting District growing the same mix of crops.

series.label: Applied mass measured as
series.note: 'burndown group' = glyphosate, paraquat, 2,4-D, dicamba, glufosinate, saflufenacil, carfentrazone - the actives that would actually substitute for the seedbed tillage pass, and therefore the sharpest available test of the hypothesised trade-off.

annotations.text: Pooled: a county at the 75th percentile of no-till (60%) carries 15.3% more glyphosate per hectare than one at the 25th (18%).
Within the same Crop Reporting District and crop mix: -2.3%. The trade-off disappears, and the point estimate changes sign.
Geography alone (row 3) removes the whole association; crop mix alone (row 4) enlarges it. The two confounders push in opposite directions, so 'partially controlled' is not a safe halfway house.

Crop mix alone explains R2 = 0.535 of county log herbicide intensity. USGS EPest county estimates are built by multiplying Crop Reporting District survey rates by county crop acreage (Thelin & Stone 2013), so this axis partly measures the crop-acreage input rather than an independent observation of spraying.
Within-CRD Spearman rho computed separately in 204 districts: median -0.059, IQR -0.400 to +0.240; 45 districts above +0.3, 60 below -0.3. There is no single national sign.
Same exercise with cover-crop share instead of no-till: -13.4% per +10 pp pooled (t = -9.0), -0.9% (t = -0.8) fully controlled. Both the apparent penalty and the apparent benefit are geography.

source_note: USDA NASS Census of Agriculture 2017 (county tillage and cover-crop acreage, harvested cropland, crop acreage) and USGS Pesticide National Synthesis Project EPest-low county estimates for 2017, California excluded on both sides. 2,087 counties holding 95.4% of national harvested cropland and 96.5% of national applied herbicide mass. Herbicide classification taken from NASS's own DOMAINCAT_DESC chemical classes. Cross-sectional association only; no causal claim.
